learning_outcomes.text: Acquire technical and design skills related to the study, selection, and sizing of fluid-driven motive and operating machines.
Analyze energy systems and their components using first and second principles.
Understand the performance and plant schemes of steam engine, gas, and mixed gas-steam plants, internal combustion engines, nuclear, and renewable energy sources.

syllabus_topics: Efflux in rotary and stator conduits of compressible and incompressible fluids
Axial, centrifugal, and reciprocating compressors and pumps
Recalls of thermodynamics and related principles
Recalls of fluid dynamics, momentum, and energy
Theory of similitude and dimensional analysis
Flow in nozzles and in rotor and stator cascades of turbomachines
Velocity triangles, work exchange between fluid and blade, degree of reaction, blading efficiency, notable degrees of reaction
Compressible fluid motive and operating turbomachines: rotor and stator components of steam and gas turbines and centrifugal and axial compressors, multistage solutions
Incompressible fluid motive and operating turbomachines: Pelton, Francis, and Kaplan hydraulic turbines, centrifugal and axial pumps
Machines inserted in a circuit, in series and in parallel
Volumetric, reciprocating, and rotary compressors and expanders
Free-flow motive and operating machines: introduction to wind turbines and propellers
Recalls of thermodynamics, first and second principles, Carnot effect, multiplicity of sources and Clausius
Exergy, calculation of exergetic efficiency with direct and inverse methods
Performance and components of 2-stroke and 4-stroke engines
Introduction to combustion and pollutant control
assessment_rules: The written exam consists of two numerical questions on plant and component sizing, with a minimum score of 15/30. The oral exam consists of two open questions on plants and/or components, with a minimum score of 18/30.
bibliography: V. Dossena et al., Macchine a fluido, Città Studi Edizioni, 2° edizione, 2020
S. Stecco, G. Manfrida, "Impianti di conversione energetica", Pitagora
degree: Corso di laurea in Ingegneria meccanica (L-9)
